claim: Unassisted pure discovery learns less than explicit instruction on average (d about -0.38 over 108 studies); the penalty is largest against worked examples (-0.63).
agent_test: Run a no-plan free-explore arm vs a worked-example or plan-given arm at equal tokens on the same item set; compare accuracy.

claim: Guided or enhanced discovery (scaffolds, feedback, self-explanation, worked examples) beats other instruction (d about 0.25-0.30); the benefit comes from the guidance, not from discovery itself.
agent_test: Compare free chain-of-thought vs guided step prompts with checkpoints at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Computer-based scaffolding in problem-centred STEM teaching helps on average (g 0.39-0.46), but credible intervals are wide and the effect varies by scaffold type.
agent_test: Not directly testable; use as a prior that scaffold type matters more than scaffold presence.

claim: Metacognitive and strategic scaffolds beat conceptual scaffolds and question prompts (g 0.38 and 0.35 vs 0.13 and 0.08).
agent_test: Ablate: strategy hint vs concept hint vs question prompt inserted at the same step, equal tokens.

claim: Fading, the defining feature of scaffolding, is rarely implemented and its benefit is unproven: no moderator difference in one meta-analysis, a small edge for fade-and-add in another, and unfaded scaffolds did better in a 2015 one.
agent_test: Compare fixed support, fade-after-success and no fade on a multi-item stream at equal tokens.

claim: Contingent tutoring (Wood, Wood, Middleton 1978) did not replicate in a large preregistered direct replication (N=285): the effect on later independent solving was not reproduced.
agent_test: Compare contingent vs fixed-level hints at equal tokens; do not assume contingency wins.

claim: Direct instruction produced more learners who mastered control of variables than discovery, yet learners who got there either way transferred equally well (path independence).
agent_test: Check whether a taught procedure vs a self-found one differ on transfer items for the agent.

claim: Unrestricted LLM help raises practice scores but lowers later unaided performance; a guardrailed tutor (hints, no answers, teacher solutions) removes the harm. Detail: practice +48% (GPT Base) and +127% (GPT Tutor); unaided exam -17% for GPT Base, -0.004 (ns) for GPT Tutor, so guardrails remove the harm but add no gain; GPT Base was right only 51% of the time.
schema_part: G (no answer copying; hint before answer)
agent_test: Scaffold-with-hints vs answer-given mode, then an unaided eval on the next item batch.

claim: Restricting AI use to guided stepwise help improved no-help quiz scores in a small non-randomised study, but a larger preregistered study found no gain from forced independent-first study.
agent_test: Compare attempt-first then hint vs immediate hint at equal tokens.

claim: A step-ordered LLM tutor with solutions in the prompt beat in-class active learning (0.63 SD, N=194); sequencing had to move into code because prompts alone drifted out of order. The paper reports this as a design observation; it gives no prompt-only vs code ablation and no token cost.
agent_test: Test prompt-only vs code-enforced step order for state transitions, equal tokens.

claim: Hints from an LLM given to human tutors raised student mastery by 4 pp (9 pp for weaker tutors) and moved tutors toward guiding questions over giving the answer.
agent_test: Test whether weak-model plus expert-style scaffold gains more than strong-model plus scaffold.

claim: Decomposing a problem into ordered easier subproblems with earlier answers fed forward gives large length-generalisation gains over chain-of-thought (SCAN 99.7 vs 16; last-letter L=12 74 vs 32-38) and on easily split reading tasks (DROP 82.45 vs 74.77, 73.42 vs 59.56), but only small gains on GSM8K (62.39 vs 60.87; gain only on 5+ step problems, 45.23 vs 39.07; CoT was better on 2-step problems, 76.68 vs 74.53).
agent_test: Replicate decompose-then-solve vs CoT with a current model at equal tokens; all numbers are from code-davinci-002 and no current-model test was found in the gap search (gap 1 open).

claim: In RL training, tiered hints given only on zero-reward hard problems, delivered incrementally and withheld early, raise pass@1; hints from step 0 hurt (hint dependency).
agent_test: Ablate hint tiers (knowledge, plan, solution) and incremental vs whole delivery at inference time, equal tokens.

claim: In RL training, hint dosage matters: aiming for about 50% rollout accuracy per problem works best (SEELE derives this from gradient signal), and whole-solution hints are weaker than layered hints. At inference, the one dose curve found (prefix hints, GSM8K) rises broadly with hint length and most items need none; no inference-time test of the 50% rule exists.
agent_test: Pick hint length by prior-attempt success rate vs fixed length at equal tokens (not yet tested for prompting).

claim: Guidance helps novices and can hurt or waste effort for experts (expertise reversal). Machine echo is mixed: Scaf-GRPO gain was +44% on a math base model but +5.9% on a long-CoT distilled model, and explicit CoT or exemplars add little on reasoning-mode or strong models (GPQA: o3-mini +0.029, o4-mini +0.031, Gemini Flash 2.5 -0.033; DeepSeek-R1 says few-shot degrades), but other work finds CoT still helps distilled reasoning models in 72% of cases and next-step hints lift distilled models on AIME.
schema_part: S0 mode: scale support to model strength
agent_test: Scaffold on/off across strong and weak models at equal tokens; expect an interaction.

claim: LLM tutors told to follow pedagogy (do not give the answer, scaffold) are preferred by experts, yet solving ability does not make a good tutor and scaffolding quality drops on long dialogs for most models.
agent_test: Check whether a withhold-the-answer rule persists across long runs of steps.

claim: Training a tutor with a penalty on leaking the solution trades some student gain for less leakage (solve-rate gain falls from 36.2% to 21.2% as the penalty rises).
agent_test: Tune how strictly final answers are barred before verification.

claim: LLM-written hints can match human hints for learning gain, but about a third are faulty; majority vote over samples cuts error to 0-13%.
agent_test: Sample hints n times and vote vs a single hint, equal tokens.

claim: Withholding direct answers raises frustration: students liked the inquiry style but rated the agent as not understanding them (2.69 of 5), and human tutors overrode Socratic drafts when they frustrated learners.
schema_part: S0 mode (when to switch from probe to tell)
agent_test: Add an escape rule: after K failed probes give the next step; compare with no escape.

claim: An LLM peer agent shifted from probing to suggesting as mastery rose (logged fading), but the outcome benefit of the shift was not tested. A second logged-fading system (Copa) shows the same: fading is observed, outcome benefit untested.
agent_test: Do not copy without an outcome test.

claim: Guided play beats direct instruction on some early skills (shape knowledge g=0.63, task switching 0.40) and free play on spatial vocabulary; no difference on most outcomes.
agent_test: Not testable on an LLM.

claim: Kirschner, Sweller and Clark (2006) is an argument with no pooled effect size; the main reply (Hmelo-Silver et al. 2007) says problem- and inquiry-based learning are scaffolded, so the dispute is partly about definitions.
agent_test: Define minimal guidance operationally before testing.

claim: Explicit step-by-step prompting has little value for dedicated reasoning models and a mixed value for non-reasoning models: the average rises a little but some easy questions get lost, and time rises 20-80% (reasoning) or 35-600% (non-reasoning). Variants including 'decompose the problem' made no meaningful difference.
schema_part: S0 mode: scaffold on only for models that need it
agent_test: Scaffold on/off by model class at equal tokens on the schema's own tasks. d04 finds CoT still helps distilled reasoning models (72% of cases), so run it per model, not by rule.

claim: At inference, a hint made of the first part of a stronger model's solution lifts a smaller model, rising broadly with hint length (Llama-3.1-8B on GSM8K 84.8 to 95.2 over 0-90%), and 80.6% of GSM8K items need no hint; next-step hints without the answer lift small reasoning models on MATH-500 (56.76 to 77.03) and AIME-2024 (0 to 44.83).
agent_test: Compare no hint, next-step hint and prefix hint at equal tokens with a verified hint source. Caveat: hints come from a stronger model; the agent has no stronger model.

claim: A model cannot reliably verify its own answer without an outside signal: intrinsic self-correction lowered accuracy (GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 after two rounds; GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 41.8) while oracle labels lifted GPT-3.5 GSM8K to 95.5; self-consistency beat debate at equal response counts (88.2 vs 83.0 at 9).
agent_test: Check self-written hints with a vote over fresh samples or an executable test, not with a re-read by the same model; measure token cost per hint.

claim: A contingent LLM tutor (help rises after failure, fades on take-up) matched a question-only tutor on demand, gave full answers in 1 of 16 sessions vs 1 of 6, and frustrated learners less than the question-only tutor, with load unchanged (131 adults, 393 sessions, within-subject); later unaided learning was not measured.
agent_test: Contingent vs fixed support at equal tokens with a delayed unaided test; the human contingency replication (K06) failed, so do not assume a learning gain.

claim: No study was found that tests fading or withdrawing scaffolds across a stream of items for a model or its memory, or that compares fade-after-success with a fixed schedule for an LLM. Human fading evidence is contested (K05).
agent_test: Own experiment: fixed schedule vs fade-after-success on an item stream with a later unaided test.

claim: No measured test of a stop-probing-and-tell escape rule was found; the nearest evidence is that the contingent tutor gave away fewer full answers than an assistant yet frustrated less than a question-only tutor (K26).
agent_test: Escape after K failed probes vs never vs always tell; measure solved rate, tokens and later unaided accuracy.
